bindaddress.description: IP address the Burp server binds to (e.g., 0.0.0.0 for all interfaces, or a specific IP).

port.description: TCP port the server listens on.

storage_dir.description: Base directory where client backups are stored. Must be writable by the burp user.

max_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous client connections. Increase for many concurrent backups.

allow_delete.description: Whether to allow clients to delete their own backups. Set to false in production to prevent accidental data loss.

compression.description: Whether to compress backup data. Enable to save storage; disable for faster transfers on CPU-limited systems.

ca_crt.description: Path to the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate for TLS.

server_crt.description: Path to the server certificate (signed by the CA).

server_key.description: Path to the server private key.

ca_crl.description: Path to the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) file (optional). Leave empty if unused.

clients.description: List of authorized Burp clients. Each client is defined by a name and certificate information.

name.description: Unique name/identifier for the client (used in client config as `name = ...`).

cert_cn.description: Common Name (CN) in the client's certificate (case-sensitive match required), or IP if using IP-based auth.

backup_dir.description: Optional subdirectory under storage_dir where this client’s backups are isolated. Must be a relative path (e.g., `clients/client1`).

password.description: Optional plaintext password for non-TLS password auth. Not used if certs are enabled. Prefer certificate auth in production.

allowed_ips.description: List of allowed source IP addresses/CIDR blocks (e.g., ['192.168.1.0/24']). Restricts connections to these networks.

allow_clients.description: Fallback list of allowed clients by certificate CN or IP (if no per-client block matches). Useful for simple setups. If empty, defaults to allowing all.

log_file.description: Path to the server log file.

log_file_level.description: Verbosity of file logging: 0=errors, 1=warnings, 2=info, 3=debug. Recommend 1 for production.
